text:
elaine_support: Hey team, ACME reported a sudden drop in embeddings throughput this morning. vectors/sec down ~4x since 08:30 UTC, tokens/sec for generation endpoints okay. They also saw intermittent 429s from our API while token billing looked normal. Attaching logs and dashboard links.
jon_eng_ml: thanks for flagging. do we have an example request pattern? batch sizes, dims?

elaine_support: sample request from customer (anonymized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "embed-large-v2",
  "input": ["short text", "much longer text ... up to ~2000 chars"],
  "user": "acme-corp"
}
```
They send mixed-length arrays. historically vectors/sec ~1500/s, now ~350/s.

maria_runtime: timeline? any recent rollout? autosplit batching landed last week to reduce long-tail latency. Could be splitting logic.

jon_eng_ml: autosplit splits by token budget not by embedding vector dim. for embeddings we have to coalesce similar-dim requests otherwise we fall back to micro-batches. maybe mixed-length arrays cause many micro-batches.

lucas_sre: observability: gpu mem spikes correlating with request bursts at 08:32. queue depth on embed workers rose to 3x, worker-side backpressure triggered 429s. link: https://console.redwood/dashboards/embeds/cluster-3?from=08:00&to=09:00

elaine_support: customer also saw billing counter for API calls increase ~2.5x at the same window — likely more requests generated by autosplit internal splits.

priya_product: can we repro with local traffic? quick script to simulate their mix?

jon_eng_ml: yes, here's a quick repro script (python):
```python
import requests
URL = "https://api.redwood.io/v1/embeddings"
HEADERS = {"Authorization":"Bearer REPRO_KEY", "Content-Type":"application/json"}
payloads = ["short", "short2", "long..."*200]
for i in range(2000):
    r = requests.post(URL, json={"model":"embed-large-v2","input":payloads})
    if i%200==0:
        print(i, r.status_code)
```
This reproduces degraded vectors/sec locally against test cluster when autosplit enabled.

maria_runtime: looking at runtime traces: autosplit path creates N sub-requests per incoming request; the path accidentally bypasses our batching aggregator so each sub-request goes into separate micro-queue. that explains kernel-launch overhead and gpu thrash.

lucas_sre: adding more: KV cache churn observed — embeddings pipeline copies context when autosplit triggers, increasing GPU mem churn which forces small batch sizes. Combined effect = reduced token/vectors throughput and queue saturation -> 429.

priya_product: what's a quick mitigation we can offer ACME?

jon_eng_ml: short-term: disable autosplit for their org or pin to static batching config. config flag: `embedding.autosplit.enabled=false` per-tenant. Also increase `batch_window_ms` to 50 and set `max_batch_size` to 128. That should force larger coalesced batches and reduce extra backend calls.

elaine_support: can we patch and roll per-tenant toggle? I can push a change if eng approves.

maria_runtime: yes we have per-tenant rollout toggles. I'll flip for acme in staging and run the repro.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: rollout/disable-autosplit-for-acme -> staging (build 2026.03.17-77)

maria_runtime: staging repro shows vectors/sec back to expected ~1400/s and 429s gone. GPU mem stable.

jon_eng_ml: good. root cause summary: autosplit logic intended to reduce latency for very long inputs ended up splitting embedding requests into variable-length subcalls that bypassed the main batch aggregator, causing many micro-batches, KV cache churn, and higher request counts -> GPU saturation and 429s.

lucas_sre: follow-ups:
- add validation to autosplit to avoid bypassing batch aggregator for embeddings
- add metric for internal-subrequest-rate per-tenant
- rate-limit internal splits to avoid billing explosion
- run load test with mixed-length payloads in CI

priya_product: we'll notify the customer and offer a credit for the extra call volume. liaise with finance for billing flag.

elaine_support: notes for postmortem: summarize timeline, rollback action (disable autosplit for acme), mitigation, and long-term fixes from lucas. I'll draft and ping for review. :thumbsup:

jon_eng_ml: one more repro note — if you want exact logs set env `REDWOOD_BATCH_DEBUG=1` on worker and collect `worker-*.log` for the 08:30 window. include trace id header `X-Trace-Id` from acme sample.

maria_runtime: adding an immediate hotfix: ensure autosplit hits the same batching codepath (PR opened), will request expedited review.

elaine_support: thanks all — will update ACME after staging verifies.
